cap: Work down from a positive hCG: check stability first, then let transvaginal ultrasound locate the pregnancy. A yolk sac in the uterus confirms an intrauterine pregnancy, an adnexal mass with an empty uterus means ectopic, and nothing seen is a pregnancy of unknown location, sorted by the discriminatory zone and a repeat hCG 48 hours later. The bottom strip shows when each ultrasound milestone should appear.
teach: The order of the questions matters. Stability comes first because a ruptured ectopic kills by bleeding, and no test result changes the need for surgery. Location comes next because methotrexate given to a normal intrauterine pregnancy would end a wanted pregnancy. Only then does viability decide between waiting and treating a loss.
